land.text: 'Matsya was eventually conquered by the empire of Magadha'

successors.note: The page names only 'the empire of Magadha', undated; its infobox ends Matsya at c. 350 BCE. Cliopatria's Nanda Empire shape from -333 holds the whole country, and the Shaishunaga shape before it holds none of it, so -349..-334 is a gap in Cliopatria. The Shaishunaga dossier should carry the -350 gain and pass the land to the Nandas (c. 345 BCE). Reviewer sa-01-c (2026-10-18): counterpart changed from nanda-empire to magadha-shaishunaga-dynasty, because the Nanda Empire page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire) has 'Established: c. 345 BCE', after this c. 350 BCE end, and the Shaishunaga dynasty page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaishunaga_dynasty; 'Established: 413 BCE', 'Disestablished: 345 BCE') lists Matsya under 'Preceded by'.

capitals.name: Viratanagara (Bairat)
capitals.note: 'The capital of Matsya was Viratanagara, which corresponds to the modern-day Bairat in Jaipur district of Rajasthan.' Coordinates approximate and mine: Bairat is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: Matsya: 'Most of the kingdom comprised parts of present-day North-eastern Rajasthan', with 'the Sarasvati river and the forests skirting it as its western border, and its southern boundaries being the hills near the Chambal River', Kuru to the north and Surasena to the east

keyframe_review.note: -600..-451. The page gives no area. Cliopatria's 5,220 km2 disc (bbox 75.68-76.63E 27.03-27.87N, centroid 76.17E 27.43N, in the Alwar-Jaipur country) lies inside the 'North-eastern Rajasthan' the page names; my correction keeps the disc and adds 50 km round Alwar and 60 km round Jaipur (about 21,000 km2), a guess at the size that the page does not support with a figure. Bairat, the capital, is in Jaipur district.

Cliopatria's Shaishunaga shape for -404 holds none of the Matsya disc, and the Nanda shape from -333 holds all of it, so without this keyframe the land would be stateless from -404 to -334.

region.text: Matsya, which the Anguttara Nikaya included among the sixteen Mahajanapadas, a monarchy round Viratanagara

ledger.note: 600 BCE: Matsya enters the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas. The infobox gives 'Established: c. 1400 BCE' and the page names the Mahajanapadas as 'the most powerful states of India immediately before the birth of the Buddha' without a year; -600 is Cliopatria's first year, so the year is a bridge. Its earlier life (the Battle of the Ten Kings in the Rigveda, undated) is not drawn.

350 BCE: Magadha conquers Matsya. 'Matsya was eventually conquered by the empire of Magadha' and the infobox has 'Disestablished: c. 350 BCE'; the page gives no date for the conquest and 'The later history of Matsya is not known'. The year is the infobox's, the counterpart is the Magadha of c. 350 BCE, ruled by the Shaishunagas. Reviewer sa-01-c (2026-10-18): counterpart changed from nanda-empire to magadha-shaishunaga-dynasty, because the Nanda Empire page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_Empire) has 'Established: c. 345 BCE', after this c. 350 BCE end, and the Shaishunaga dynasty page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaishunaga_dynasty; 'Established: 413 BCE', 'Disestablished: 345 BCE') lists Matsya under 'Preceded by'.

certainty.note: Only rivers, forest and hills bound the country (the Sarasvati to the west, the Chambal hills to the south); no frontier with Kuru or Surasena is given.

sources.title: Matsya (tribe)
sources.note: North-eastern Rajasthan, Viratanagara (Bairat), infobox c. 1400-c. 350 BCE, conquered by Magadha (undated).

notes: One page for two shapes. Not settled: (1) the Magadhan conquest is undated on the page; -350 is its infobox figure and Cliopatria's Nanda shape begins -333, leaving -349..-334 stateless in Cliopatria unless the Nanda dossier starts earlier. (2) The pre-600 life (infobox c. 1400 BCE; Rigveda; the Shatapatha Brahmana's horse sacrifice near the Sarasvati) is undated and belongs to the Vedic additions batch. (3) The page names Kuru to the north and Surasena to the east and links the Matsyas with the Caidyas (Chedi) only through the Mahabharata; no territorial event with those states is dated. (4) The Matsya Union of 1947-49 (Bharatpur, Dholpur, Alwar, Karauli) is on the page but is not evidence of the ancient extent and is not used. (5) Gazetteer names wanted: Bairat / Viratanagara (place), Matsya (region). (6) No wars listed.
